Nonetheless, some hardy settlers from our metropole have gone all the way to these stormy islands to settle, and have established a few little fishing communities. A vessel that had been traveling through the Ishnapt has recently pulled into $CAPITAL$ and told us a little bit of the goings on there. They tell us of the ferocious storms that come down from the north, and that the settlers and native Mjhm’an build their fanzas and cottages on the lee sides of the mountains that tower out of these islands. They tell us of the strange, pygmy fatty molluscs that the settlers fish for in the northern waters, and the chewy roots grown there. The local settlers have been calling these places ‘Druboukiru’ (Thundering island’) and ‘Fundrouukiru’ (the ‘Cabbagefruit Islands’, from its abundant growth). The Admiralty proposes updating our maps.
This should look nicer than native gibberish.
Who's going to look at this place, anyway?

The arid Kovan coast is home to a number of petty principalities ruled by braggadocious Rechktists princes. Our merchants typically cross by these coasts when trading with the wealthier powers of the south, and little heed is paid to the Kovan lands, barring a small trade in wool and Ishahfazhi weaponry. Regrettably, however, the Rechtist princes still oppress sailors who wash up on their shores with slavery and worse, and trade them south to the great powers. Things took a poor turn in our relations recently: a redemptorist religious association that was quartered in a Kovan city was forcibly suppressed and the clerics themselves sold into slavery! One man managed to make it back to $CAPITAL$, to tell his tale of horror, and has now got the foreign ministry and the press up in arms! The government thinks it prudent to finally put an end to the slave raiding from these dangerous shores, and the public seems behind them.
Good heavens, we've got to get these savages under order!
All that for some damned hubbub in the wastes...?

We have a number of diminutive possessions on the Kovan Coast, a few ancient old cities garrisoned with shabby soldiers and a few forts to keep the restive tribesmen from causing problems. The principle trouble is that the worshipers of the ‘Bright Eyed God’, the Rechktists, the schismatic Momurists, consider temporal power of the Rechtian faithful religiously important. Willing to go to great lengths to achieve their Gottstaat, we regularly have to engage in small expeditions to suppress extremist anti-imperialists in the bush and hills, and even in desert holdfasts. Recently, we’ve been dealing with a particularly well equipped, sly rebel: Isio x'Emechk, and, to our great alarm, we’ve found that a local independent Kovan lord has been supporting and protecting him! After a recent battle, he fled to the court of this impudent lord, and the colonial governorate and the foreign office are asking that we prosecute the war into these neighbouring lands.
For heaven's sake, we've got to catch him!
And I am sure the foreign minister isn't going to sign the cheque.

The great eastern continent, Bafozh, named so by the Gashdzii term for east - ‘Bafa’ - a pre-Kadkohic vengeful sun god. It is the largest of all six major landmasses and also boasts most of the most impressive natural formations. Marked by its primitive stage of development, empty landscapes, vast mountain ranges, deep valleys, and endless forests, it represents at once opportunity and freedom as well as the great unknown. The current interest in Bafozh, whether topographical, military, anthropological, or scientific merits continuous interest in outfitting exploratory missions to the uncharted interior of the continent. The foreign office and the military high command suggest that we find some likely young captain, a cartographer or two, and some soldiers to send into these lands.
No, minister, we cannot indulge your interest in adventure stories.

Our recent expedition into the heart of Bafozh has returned to $CAPITAL$ and they report the most strange and shocking tales! In the heart of the southern forests, labouring through strange taiga and dense boreal forests, our captain explains that he kept running across strange folk who his guides explained were Juewaeg faithful bringing captives for rites near lake Geshe, sometimes for thousands of miles. He eventually decided to follow a group of these faithful to Geshe. On the banks of lake Geshe he witnessed the most fantastical rites. The Lords of Hamog, the masters of these lands, grow rich by the tribute and captives brought by the faithful across the southern forests, and oversee the bloodletting of the many hundreds of captives into the waters of the pristine forest lake, to the ecstatic joy of the thronging masses of Juewaeg of all races and cultures who cluster there. But shockingly, the explorer was asked to offer his own sacrifice, to see the rites! He relates that…
… he presented a coolie of his own expedition to the Lord of Hamog!
… he bought a slave and gave it for the sacrifice.
… he refused these rites and fled from the rage of the Hamogine king!

The great eastern continent, Bafozh, named so by the Gashdzii term for east - ‘Bafa’ - a pre-Kadkohic vengeful sun god. It is the largest of all six major landmasses and also boasts most of the most impressive natural formations. Marked by its primitive stage of development, empty landscapes, vast mountain ranges, deep valleys, and endless forests, it represents at once opportunity and freedom as well as the great unknown. In recent years, a number of those in the natural and social sciences have expressed interest in sending an expedition to the dense reaches of this largely unexplored continent. At a recent colloquium and soiree in a fine academic establishment in $CAPITAL$, the Bafozh exploration society proposed, in the presence of the minister for the sciences, a military-explorative mission into the heart of Bafozh. Since we ostensibly have colonial interests in this region, state geographers would be certainly interested in charting these lands.
What a splended idea! Outfit an expendition at once!
What could be out there but barbarous anthrophages and bad weather?

Our recent expedition into the heart of Bafozh has returned to $CAPITAL$ and they report the most wonderful discovery! In the Mountains of Boshbish (which has been bastardized to ‘Bobit’ in the mouth of our captain and his soldiers), amongst the Behshi pastoralists, our explorer discovered the most strange ancient ruins. It appears that many centuries or even millenia ago there was some sort of developed and settled civilisation that raised a number of forts and strange petroglyphs. Shockingly, the size of these buildings implies that these people must have been profoundly tall and large, perhaps extreme specimens of the large Bafozhi folk known to us today. In any case, archeologists, linguists, and classicists are extremely excited to study this newly identified ancient civilisation.

Several years ago we sent an explorer and some men into the interior of Bafozh to chart these lands and spread the influence of our great state. He has not made any contact with us for a long time and seems, for all intents and purposes, to be lost. Whether he was eaten by savages, starved to death in the vast interior, or died in some natural disaster, the money spent on provisions and ships seems to have been a waste.
Poor chap, tsk tsk. Can we find out who approved this?

Pruub, the sweet, soporific, euphoric oils of the Magoupt plant is indigenous to the Poumnian lands and the Poudwouvas river delta. It has, for millennia, practically been solely grown in this region: only there are the soils appropriate, the swampy rivers carry the appropriate mix of fresh water and heavy sediments, and the clime remains ideal. Now, however, with new pumping technologies, our industrial agronomists believe some swampland in our territories could be suitable to Pruub cultivation. A certain agricultural firm has come to our government with a scheme to plant Pruub, and wants a government monopoly and subsidies for this purpose.
Grant these fellows their monopoly, and get planting!
No, what we produce in $PROVINCENAME$ is too valuable.

'I left my son out in the sun, with the ruminants... and I saw a black cloud gathering far distant on the horizon... before I knew it, it was too late. All that remained of the fields, the cattle, and my son, was bones and chaff.' Such were the scenes of devastation where the locusts were first spawning. A local region is now facing a deadly threat of a plague of ravenous, omnivorous, monstrously large locusts! Their evil red eyes glare out of their shiny carapaces, glistening in the humid, thick air, their eager mandibles ready to devour anything in their path. The wet, warm weather drives them into a spawning frenzy, and their terrible number grows hourly in exponential orders. Their ominous drone resonates across the fields, and the people, with little left for them to do, cower and pray that these creatures only eat their fields, and not the very flesh off their bones.
There's no telling where those damned things will strike!

The locusts have come to $PROVINCENAME$! They have visted theses lands with their terrible appetites and left terrible devestation in their wake! Everywhere fields have been entirely destroyed, cattle and livestock devoured in the very pastures, houses and homes themselves have been gnawed upon, seed reserves have been torn to bits: little remains of the once prosperous agricultural region. People are leaving these lands in great numbers, as it seems it will be a long time until these regions recover their former prosperity, and those that stay eke out a miserable, desperate existence, trying to hastily cultivate their plots, but is expected that many will suffer famine and malnutrition. People are petitioning the government for relief of their burdens and suffering, more than whatever reserves local authorites can provide. Should the national government step in?
We must try to relieve this region.
We cannot afford to provide these people with any more aid.
Locust Plague Comes to an End

The terrible locust plague that has struck one of our regions has seemingly ended. Having devastated most viable parts of this area, it seems that the swarm has burnt itself out. With no food remaining, and their brief lives coming to an end, they now die in their millions. Their hideous corpses litter the fields, and carrion birds pick at their fattened bodies. Even desperate farmers come to harvest the bodies to eat in desperation. The region itself remains devastated, and the abatement of this plague, while a relief, comes to a land that has lost everything already.

All the time in $PROVINCENAME$, now, you have hear the thunder of metal on metal and the bellowing of the locomotive, as newly laid railway track carries these new machines into the heart of our country. But the people are in uproar! They say these tracks had been built through the lands of ancient farms, and that this machine disturbs the traditional bounds of villages, cattle-driving paths, scaries the birds, and frightens the whole town as it thunders through. They've appealed to their local 'Roots-Man', the Tehuhrite Holyman who lives in the roots of an ancient tree on the bounds of a large provincial town. He has consdiered their pleas, and has ruled that the railway causes too much disturbance! Given the Tehuhrite faith of our country, we are under great pressure to oblige with his religious-judicial perpective.
If the holy man says so...
What nonsense! That was a massive investment!

In $PROVINCENAME$ we have a large naval instillation. This harbour and drydock protects military ships, supplies them, and host a number of support vessels, as well as employs locals to build massive new vessels for our grand fleet. However, it causes great distress for the local fishermen. They say the huge vessels going out to sea disturb the shoals, the waves capsize their little vessels, and even the tugs tear up their nets. They have appealed to a local 'roots man', a Tehuhrite holyman who has lived much of his life stationary in the roots of a tree, fed and watered by locals. He has pronounced that this community has fished here for centuries, and that their rights of use take priority over those of the navy! We must decide what to do.
His holiness and his verdict must be honoured!
The Admiralty would be furious. Not a chance.

Our state has been wracked with a great calamity recently. In the substantial chaos that has afflicted our provinces, the various wretched bonded folk - the slaves, thralls, serfs, prisoners, hereditary servants, have come to control a substantial section of territory. Massacring their masters and setting fire to the great houses, these lands have become a wasteland of anarchy and delusional ideas of equality, brotherhood, and liberty. Even more preposterously, some of their leaders have had the audacity to proclaim a ‘free commonwealth’, and have begun seeking peaceable arrangements with other powers, acting as if they were sovereign! These are dark days for our state indeed, and the question remains to be asked about what ought to be done with this rebellious “state”.
Get these lands to order, right now!
Our various colonial administrators work tirelessly to make sure our colonial policy is being correctly implemented in suitable overseas departments.
Tally-ho, chaps, let's get a move on.
